US-95 · between Las Vegas and Reno · elevation 5,686 ft

Goldfield

Fall out of the Milky Way, through 120 years of boom and bust, and land in the middle of nowhere.

Plan a stopBusiness directory

Tonight · south-east edge of town

The International Car Forest of the Last Church

More than forty cars, trucks and buses stand nose-down in the desert. Mark Rippie buried the first one in 2002. It is free, it never closes, and the sky out here is this dark.

Rolling the years back

Every empty lot was a building once.

Watch the town come back up out of the ground.

1905 · 925 North Fifth Avenue

The Santa Fe Saloon

Hubert Maxgut built it out past the business district, up toward the mines. That distance is why it is still standing. It has poured drinks every year since.

Inside

Same bar. Same wood stove.

The original bar is still the one you lean on. Goldfield’s oldest business in continuous operation is also the best place in town to hear what happened next.

1908 · looking north-east to Columbia Mountain

The largest city in Nevada

About 20,000 people. Five banks, five newspapers, three railroads, and a four-storey hotel of granite and brick. The mines sit under the mountain; the hundred-stamp mill starts dropping in December.

Main Street & Crook Avenue

Burros, bullion and eighty bartenders

Tex Rickard’s Northern Saloon was said to need eighty men behind the bar. In 1906 he staged the Gans–Nelson title fight here: forty-two rounds in the September sun.

September 1913

The flood

A flash flood came down the wash and carried off hundreds of buildings. The mines were already three years past their peak.

July 6, 1923

The first fire

It started with a moonshine still. By nightfall some twenty-five blocks of the business district were ash.

September 29, 1924

The second fire

It took the Goldfield News building and the Montezuma Club, much of what the first one had missed.

Today · population about 225

What the boom left behind

The hotel, the courthouse, the high school and the firehouse still stand. Between them: art cars, a house built of bottles, wild burros, and a truck that should have stopped.

Gemfield · four miles out · a dollar a pound

Get lost in the middle of nowhere.

Dig your own chalcedony until the light goes. Then look up.

Add Goldfield to your route

Plan the stop

You are driving past it anyway.

US-95 runs straight through Goldfield on Crook Avenue. Most people slow to 25 and keep going. Pull over instead: pick how long you have and take the list with you.

  • 28 mifrom Tonopah
  • ~67 mifrom Beatty
  • ~185 mifrom Las Vegas
  • ~260 mifrom Reno

How long have you got?

Distances other than Tonopah are approximate; check your map. Fuel: the Goldfield Truck Stop opened in April 2026, and Tonopah and Beatty remain the sure things. Mobile signal is patchy between towns. Carry water.
